reuse.why: Builds on the existing getScheduledAmount and the existing getApproxNumberThreshold tolerance helper, and routes four of the five copies through getScheduledAmount; schedule-template uses only the sub-helpers.

duplication.why: The five midpoint copies collapse into shared helpers, but schedule-template keeps its own op dispatch (isbetween/isapprox/is) that duplicates the dispatch inside getScheduledAmount.

placement.why: The rule and its parts live in shared/schedules.ts next to the other schedule helpers; expectedAmount is produced in scheduleModel.toExternal, the API mapping layer.

scope.why: Edits are confined to the amount rule, its call sites, the API model, tests and release notes for the requested steps.

maintainability.why: Clear named helpers with tests; the loosely typed op?: string parameter and the separate dispatch in schedule-template mean a future rule change must be checked in two places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: createScheduleList in packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/schedule-template.ts dispatches on amountCondition.op itself and calls getRangeWorstCase/getApproxWorstCase instead of getScheduledAmount(value, false, op)

disguised_duplication.where: schedule-template.ts re-expresses getScheduledAmount's op dispatch as a nested ternary over getRangeWorstCase/getApproxWorstCase, a reshaped copy of the shared function's branching.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter and an op==='isapprox' branch; schedule-template.ts createScheduleList bypasses it with its own dispatch.
